# As the columns are in Parameter ID format, we rename it using the parameter_mapping_details.csv
# Also there are two type of village ids, one village id is JJM defined and one village id is Census defined
# The API data has JJM defined village id but not the Census Village ids
# To attach Latitude Longitude with villages we need census village code 
# We have a mapping obtained from jjm different datasets which maps jjm village id to census village ids
In [4]:
import pandas as pd

village_file = "Data/Village_ID_df.csv" # JJM Village id to Census Village ID mapping
parameter_file = "Data/parameters_mapping_details.csv"

state_dict = {15: "Karnataka"}

# =============================================================================
# LOAD LOOKUP TABLES
# =============================================================================
village_df = pd.read_csv(village_file, low_memory=False)
village_df.columns = village_df.columns.str.strip().str.lower()
village_df["villageid"] = pd.to_numeric(village_df["villageid"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
village_df = village_df[["villageid", "census village code"]].drop_duplicates()

parameter_df = pd.read_csv(parameter_file)
parameter_df.columns = parameter_df.columns.str.strip().str.lower()
parameter_map = dict(zip(parameter_df["parameter_id"], parameter_df["parameter_name"]))

# =============================================================================
# PREPROCESS kdf
# =============================================================================
# Standardize column names
kdf.columns = kdf.columns.str.strip().str.lower()

# Add state name
kdf["stateid"] = pd.to_numeric(kdf["stateid"], errors="coerce")
kdf["statename"] = kdf["stateid"].map(state_dict)

# Merge census village code
kdf["villageid"] = pd.to_numeric(kdf["villageid"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
kdf = kdf.merge(village_df, on="villageid", how="left")

# Rename parameter columns (ParameterId_N -> actual parameter name)
rename_dict = {}
for col in kdf.columns:
    if col.startswith("parameterid_"):
        try:
            pid = int(col.split("_")[1])
            if pid in parameter_map:
                rename_dict[col] = parameter_map[pid]
        except Exception:
            pass

kdf.rename(columns=rename_dict, inplace=True)

# =============================================================================
# DATA QUALITY CHECK
# =============================================================================
total_rows = len(kdf)
print(f"Total rows: {total_rows:,}")
print()
print(list(kdf.columns))
print()

if "census village code" in kdf.columns:
    matched = kdf["census village code"].notna().sum()
    print(f"Census Village Code matched: {matched:,}/{total_rows:,} ({matched/total_rows*100:.2f}%)")

print()

if "statename" in kdf.columns:
    mapped = kdf["statename"].notna().sum()
    print(f"StateName mapped: {mapped:,}/{total_rows:,} ({mapped/total_rows*100:.2f}%)")

kdf["Month"] = kdf["test_date"].dt.month

# Remove test_date
kdf = kdf.drop(columns=["test_date"])

# Rename pollutant columns to clean names
kdf = kdf.rename(columns={
    "Fluoride (as F)": "Fluoride",

In [14]:
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap, BoundaryNorm
import pandas as pd

village_shapefile_path = 'Shapefiles Related/Village/village_modified.shp' 
village_gdf = gpd.read_file(village_shapefile_path)
village_gdf['pc11_tv_id'] = village_gdf['pc11_tv_id'].astype(int) # pc11 = pop Census 2011, Town Village Id
village_gdf.rename(columns={'pc11_tv_id':'Census Village Code'}, inplace=True)
village_gdf['Latitude'] = village_gdf['geometry'].centroid.y
village_gdf['Longitude'] = village_gdf['geometry'].centroid.x
village_gdf = village_gdf[[ 'Census Village Code', 'Latitude', 'Longitude']]
village_gdf = village_gdf.drop_duplicates(subset=['Census Village Code'], keep='first')

# state_shapefile_path = 'Shapefiles ( SHRUG )/State/state.shp' 
# state_gdf = gpd.read_file(state_shapefile_path)

village_gdf.dropna(inplace = True)
village_gdf

    kdf.groupby(
        ["statename", "villageid", "census village code", "Year", "Month"],
        as_index=False
    )
    .agg({
        **{col: "mean" for col in pollutant_cols},
        "Latitude": "first",
        "Longitude": "first"
    })
)

# Removal Code
In [29]:
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================
# 1. Keep only rows with valid coordinates
# ============================================================

kdf_work = kdf_agg.dropna(
    subset=["Latitude", "Longitude"]
).copy()

print("Original rows:", len(kdf_agg))
print("Rows with coordinates:", len(kdf_work))


# ============================================================
# 3. Get UNIQUE coordinate pairs
#    Spatial operation will only be done once per location
# ============================================================

unique_coords = (
    kdf_work[["Latitude", "Longitude"]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)

print("Unique coordinates to check:", len(unique_coords))


# ============================================================
# 4. Convert unique coordinates to GeoDataFrame
# ============================================================

coords_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    unique_coords,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(
        unique_coords["Longitude"],
        unique_coords["Latitude"]
    ),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
)


# ============================================================
# 5. Convert Karnataka boundary to projected CRS
#    EPSG:32643 = UTM Zone 43N
#    Units are meters
# ============================================================

state_proj = (
    state_gdf
    .set_crs("EPSG:4326", allow_override=True)
    .to_crs("EPSG:32643")
)


# ============================================================
# 6. Create 500 meter buffer around Karnataka
# ============================================================

karnataka_boundary = state_proj.geometry.unary_union

karnataka_buffer = karnataka_boundary.buffer(500)


# ============================================================
# 7. Project points to same CRS
# ============================================================

coords_gdf = coords_gdf.to_crs("EPSG:32643")


# ============================================================
# 8. Check whether coordinates are inside
#    Karnataka + 500m buffer
# ============================================================

coords_gdf["valid"] = coords_gdf.geometry.within(
    karnataka_buffer
)

print(
    "Valid coordinates:",
    coords_gdf["valid"].sum()
)

print(
    "Invalid coordinates:",
    (~coords_gdf["valid"]).sum()
)


# ============================================================
# 9. Get valid coordinate pairs
# ============================================================

valid_coords = coords_gdf.loc[
    coords_gdf["valid"],
    ["Latitude", "Longitude"]
].copy()


# ============================================================
# 10. Filter original kdf using valid coordinates
# ============================================================

kdf_agg = kdf_agg.merge(
    valid_coords,
    on=["Latitude", "Longitude"],
    how="inner"
)


# ============================================================
# 11. Reset index
# ============================================================

kdf_agg = kdf_agg.reset_index(drop=True)


# ============================================================
# 12. Final checks
# ============================================================

print("\n-----------------------------")
print("Final rows:", len(kdf_agg))
print("Removed rows:", len(kdf_work) - len(kdf_agg))
print("-----------------------------")

print(kdf_agg)

import pandas as pd

# File paths for the final saved CSVs of each variable
variable_files = {
    'def': 'Data/Karnataka_def.csv',
    'tmax': 'Data/Karnataka_tmax.csv',
    'tmin': 'Data/Karnataka_tmin.csv',
    'wind': 'Data/Karnataka_wind.csv',
    'runoff': 'Data/Karnataka_runoff.csv',
    'ppt': 'Data/Karnataka_ppt.csv',
    'soil': 'Data/Karnataka_soil.csv'
}

# Function to read and clean individual DataFrames
def read_and_clean_csv(file_path):
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    # Drop duplicate rows, keeping only the first occurrence
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'])
    return df

# Read and clean each DataFrame
Karnataka_def_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['def'])
Karnataka_tmax_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['tmax'])
Karnataka_tmin_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['tmin'])
Karnataka_wind_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['wind'])
Karnataka_runoff_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['runoff'])
Karnataka_preci_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['ppt'])
Karnataka_soil_moisture_df = read_and_clean_csv(variable_files['soil'])

# Merge all the cleaned DataFrames on 'village ID', 'Year', and 'Month' using inner join
merged_df = Karnataka_def_df
merged_df = merged_df.merge(Karnataka_tmax_df, on=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'], how='inner')
merged_df = merged_df.merge(Karnataka_tmin_df, on=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'], how='inner')
merged_df = merged_df.merge(Karnataka_wind_df, on=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'], how='inner')
merged_df = merged_df.merge(Karnataka_runoff_df, on=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'], how='inner')
merged_df = merged_df.merge(Karnataka_preci_df, on=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'], how='inner')
merged_df = merged_df.merge(Karnataka_soil_moisture_df, on=['village ID', 'Year', 'Month'], how='inner')

# Save the merged DataFrame to a CSV file
merged_df.to_csv('Data/Karnataka_climate_data.csv', index=False)

# Display the merged DataFrame
merged_df

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from shapely.geometry import Point
from sklearn.neighbors import BallTree
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load Karnataka state boundary
state_gdf = gpd.read_file("Shapefiles Related/State/state.shp")
state_gdf = state_gdf[state_gdf['s_name'] == 'Karnataka']

# Ensure your `gdf` is a GeoDataFrame with EPSG:4326

df = kdf_agg.copy()

df['geometry'] = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(df['Longitude'], df['Latitude'])]
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(df, geometry=df['geometry'], crs="EPSG:4326")
gdf = gdf.to_crs(epsg=3857)

# Drop duplicates based on VillageId and geometry
gdf_unique = gdf.drop_duplicates(subset=['villageid', 'geometry'])

# Extract coordinates
coords = np.vstack([gdf_unique.geometry.x, gdf_unique.geometry.y]).T

# Build BallTree
tree = BallTree(coords, metric='euclidean')
indices = tree.query_radius(coords, r=100)

# Collect too-close VillageIds
too_close_ids = set()
for i, neighbors in enumerate(indices):
    if len(neighbors) > 1:
        too_close_ids.update(gdf_unique.iloc[neighbors].villageid.tolist())

# Create GeoDataFrame of removed points
removed_points = gdf[gdf['villageid'].isin(too_close_ids)]

# Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 10))
state_gdf.to_crs(epsg=3857).plot(ax=ax, color='white', edgecolor='black')
removed_points.plot(ax=ax, color='red', markersize=10, label='Removed (Too Close)')
ax.set_title("Removed Villages (Distance < 100m)")
plt.legend()
plt.xlabel("Longitude")
plt.ylabel("Latitude")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Point
from sklearn.neighbors import BallTree
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = kdf_agg.copy()

df['geometry'] = [Point(xy) for xy in zip(df['Longitude'], df['Latitude'])]
gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(df, geometry=df['geometry'], crs="EPSG:4326")
gdf = gdf.to_crs(epsg=3857)
# Project to a metric system (meters)
gdf = gdf.to_crs(epsg=3857)

# Drop duplicates based on VillageId and location to avoid redundancy in distance check
gdf_unique = gdf.drop_duplicates(subset=['villageid', 'geometry'])

# Extract coordinates in numpy array for BallTree
coords = np.vstack([gdf_unique.geometry.x, gdf_unique.geometry.y]).T

# Build BallTree to check distances efficiently
tree = BallTree(coords, metric='euclidean')

# Find all pairs within 250 meters (exclude self-pairs)
indices = tree.query_radius(coords, r=100)

# Flatten and build village pairs that are too close
too_close_ids = set()
for i, neighbors in enumerate(indices):
    if len(neighbors) > 1:
        too_close_ids.update(gdf_unique.iloc[neighbors].villageid.tolist())

# Remove these VillageIds from the original dataframe
final_gdf = gdf[~gdf['villageid'].isin(too_close_ids)]
final_gdf = final_gdf.drop(columns = ['geometry'])
final_gdf

import os
import pandas as pd
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import geopandas as gpd

# --------------------------------------------------
# Load data
# --------------------------------------------------

subbasin_gdf = gpd.read_file('Data/WFSServer (4)/CWCSUBBASIN.shp')

karnataka_wq = pd.read_csv("Data/Karnataka WQ Data with TerraClimate.csv")

# --------------------------------------------------
# Village points
# --------------------------------------------------

wq_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    karnataka_wq,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(
        karnataka_wq["Longitude"],
        karnataka_wq["Latitude"]
    ),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Karnataka boundary
# --------------------------------------------------

state_gdf = gpd.read_file(
    'Shapefiles Related/State/state.shp'
)

karnataka = state_gdf[state_gdf["s_name"] == "Karnataka"].to_crs("EPSG:4326")

# --------------------------------------------------
# Subbasins
# --------------------------------------------------

subbasin_gdf = subbasin_gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

subbasin_ktk = gpd.clip(
    subbasin_gdf[['Sub_Basin', 'geometry']],
    karnataka
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Spatial join
# --------------------------------------------------

village_ba = gpd.sjoin(
    wq_gdf,
    subbasin_ktk,
    how="left",
    predicate="intersects"
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Village-level mapping
# --------------------------------------------------
village_mapping = (
    village_ba[["villageid", "Sub_Basin"]]
    .drop_duplicates("villageid")
    .copy()
)


village_mapping

# ============================================================
# Project everything to a CRS with meters
# ============================================================

PROJECTED_CRS = "EPSG:32643"

# Unmatched village points
unmatched_gdf = wq_gdf[
    wq_gdf["villageid"].isin(unmatched_villages)
][
    ["villageid", "Latitude", "Longitude", "geometry"]
].drop_duplicates("villageid").copy()

unmatched_gdf = unmatched_gdf.to_crs(PROJECTED_CRS)


# Watershed polygons in projected CRS
subbasin_proj = subbasin_ktk[
    [
        "Sub_Basin",
        "geometry"
    ]
].copy()

subbasin_proj = subbasin_proj.to_crs(PROJECTED_CRS)

# ============================================================
# Extract watershed boundaries
# ============================================================

subbasin_edges = subbasin_proj.copy()

subbasin_edges["geometry"] = (
    subbasin_edges.geometry.boundary
)

# ============================================================
# Find nearest watershed EDGE
# ============================================================

nearest_basin = gpd.sjoin_nearest(
    unmatched_gdf,
    subbasin_edges[
        [
            "Sub_Basin",
            "geometry"
        ]
    ],
    how="left",
    distance_col="distance_m"
)

# Convert distance to km
nearest_basin["distance_km"] = (
    nearest_basin["distance_m"] / 1000
)

nearest_basin

# ============================================
# STEP 0: Imports
# ============================================
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Point

# ============================================
# STEP 1: Convert to GeoDataFrames
# ============================================

# df1: groundwater (village level)
gdf1 = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    df1,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(df1['Longitude'], df1['Latitude']),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
)

# df2: satellite grid
gdf2 = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    df2,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(df2['lon'], df2['lat']),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
)

# ============================================
# STEP 2: Reproject to metric CRS (IMPORTANT)
# ============================================
gdf1 = gdf1.to_crs(epsg=3857)
gdf2 = gdf2.to_crs(epsg=3857)

# ============================================
# STEP 3: Nearest Neighbor Spatial Join
# ============================================
gdf_merged = gpd.sjoin_nearest(
    gdf1,
    gdf2,
    how="left",
    distance_col="distance"
)

# ============================================
# STEP 4: Pick correct year values
# ============================================

def pick_year(row, prefix):
    year = int(row['Year'])
    col = f"{prefix}_{year}"
    return row[col] if col in row else None

# Assign year-specific values
gdf_merged['ntl'] = gdf_merged.apply(lambda r: pick_year(r, 'ntl'), axis=1)
gdf_merged['ndvi'] = gdf_merged.apply(lambda r: pick_year(r, 'ndvi'), axis=1)

# ============================================
# STEP 5: Clean dataset
# ============================================

# Drop unnecessary columns
drop_cols = [
    'index_right', 'system:index', '.geo',
    'ntl_2022','ntl_2023','ntl_2024',
    'ndvi_2022','ndvi_2023','ndvi_2024'
]

final_df = gdf_merged.drop(columns=[c for c in drop_cols if c in gdf_merged.columns])

# ============================================
# STEP 6: Final dataset
# ============================================


# ============================================
# STEP 7: Basic checks (IMPORTANT)
# ============================================

print("Distance summary (meters):")
print(final_df['distance'].describe())

print("\nMissing values:")
print(final_df.isna().sum())
final_df
